_expect.name: Rattlesnake Canyon Crags (including Upper and Lower Alchemist)

ca_rattlesnake_canyon_crags_including_up.blurb: A jumble of faces and blocks on the opposite side of Rattlesnake Canyon from Renaissance Crag, above Santa Barbara. Upper Alchemist is the tall headwall and Lower Alchemist the broken ground beneath it. Most of the thirteen climbs are bolted, with four trad lines mixed in, and several run to two pitches. Grades start at slab climbs in the 5.6 and 5.7 range, with the bulk at 5.9, then a few hard clip-ups at 5.11 and 5.12. The canyon feels like a maze, with cliff bands appearing unexpectedly, and the area is still being developed, with older bolts and anchors scattered about. Expect a quiet, adventurous day with good views.
ca_rattlesnake_canyon_crags_including_up.parking_note: Leave the car at the Rattlesnake Canyon trailhead and walk the canyon trail from there.

ca_race_crack_area.blurb: The first stretch of the main wall at Danland, on the edge of Sequoia National Park near Mineral King. This is mostly a trad crag with sheer, polished faces split by crack and corner systems, plus a handful of aid lines and one bolted route. Eight of the thirteen climbs are gear routes. Difficulty runs from easy 5.5 terrain through a solid middle of 5.8 to 5.11, topping out around 5.12, and several lines are two or three pitches long. The wall is newly developed, so some routes can be dirty until more traffic cleans them. A good stop for climbers comfortable placing their own protection.

ca_bb_the_jungle_gym.blurb: A secluded, dark and shady corner of the lower Merced River canyon, on the south side of the river below Yosemite Valley. Ten of the thirteen routes are trad, with two sport lines and a top-rope. The grades start around 5.8 and are concentrated in the 5.10 range, with a handful of 5.11 climbs and two at 5.12, so it suits climbers with some experience looking for steady mid-grade cracks and faces. The area sees far fewer visitors than the famous Valley walls, and the shade makes it a good option when the sun-baked cliffs nearby are too warm.

ca_split_dome_south_rock.blurb: A big dome cut by an east-west gully, right beside the Split Rocks lot in the Pinto Basin area of Joshua Tree National Park. The south rock holds a dozen or so lines, mostly trad with a few bolted options. Difficulty spans from 5.6 up through the 5.13 range, with the greatest number around 5.8 and a spread of 5.10 and 5.11 routes. The grainy surface sees little traffic, and the dome gets plenty of sun, so cooler months are the more comfortable choice. Most climbs need anchors built at the top, and descents are walk-offs. Short approach, quiet atmosphere.

ca_ap_new_diversions.blurb: A compact cragging cliff in the lower Merced River canyon, reached from the highway that runs beside the river below Yosemite Valley. Eleven of the thirteen routes are trad, with two bolted lines, and many are one to three pitches of crack and knob climbing. Grades range from an easy 5.6 through a core of 5.9 and 5.10, with a few 5.11 and 5.12 climbs for stronger parties. The cliff is shaded for roughly the first four hours after sunrise and then gets sun, so it works well as a morning stop. It sees less traffic than the better-known Valley crags, and the walk-in is about ten minutes.

ca_tall_wall_the.blurb: A tall, narrow formation in the Western Wall Area of the Alabama Hills, just outside Lone Pine in the Eastern Sierra. The wall is mostly bolted: eleven of its thirteen climbs are sport routes, with two trad lines. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with the largest group at 5.10, several easier 5.7 to 5.9 routes for warm-ups, and a couple of harder lines at the top. The Western Wall Area as a whole is known for some of the best rock and longest routes in the Hills, so this is a handy stop to combine with its neighboring crags. Expect desert rock, open views and relatively few other parties.
